summary: Upscale op applies the factor TWICE - 1.5x on a 768x1344 source yields 1728x3024 (2.25x). Root is NOT the factor and NOT the workflow: Input_Upscale_Factor has exactly one writer (PromptBoxControls.upscaleFactor, injects the raw 1.5), the sidecars for upscale_013/014/015/016 all record 1.5, node 1657 feeds only MpiGridDimensions.upscale_factor and UltimateSDUpscale.upscale_by, and the user ran the same graph in the ComfyUI browser and got the correct size. The graph is fed the WRONG IMAGE: generationSettings.mediaItems points at Media/.preview-assets/1ed8902c...png which measures 1152x2016, i.e. the 768x1344 source already enlarged 1.5x. 1152x2016 * 1.5 = 1728x3024 exactly. t2i_039's own sidecar reports pixelDimensions 768x1344 and has no previewAssets, so that file is not a full-res twin - it exists only in the content-addressed staging store. All four runs used the same hash, consistent with a deterministic pre-scale of the same source at the same factor. UNPROVEN: which code writes the pre-scaled staged copy. Start there.

User-reported context added, and it shifts the leading hypothesis. At the time of these runs the user (1) DELETED several upscale entries to make room to keep testing, and (2) at one point had a generation finishing in the ComfyUI browser while starting another in the app. (1) lines up with the MPI-225 comment above _opScopedMediaItems in generationService.js: a stale PromptBox media chip gets snapshotted into generationSettings.mediaItems and injects the wrong image, and the reference orphans once a card in that lineage is deleted. _opScopedMediaItems only filters chips whose mediaType the op does not declare - upscale DOES declare an image slot, so a stale image chip passes straight through and becomes Input_Image. That explains all four runs recording the same asset hash with a correct factor and a correct graph. (2) is unlikely alone: a one-off race would not produce the SAME hash at dispatch on four consecutive runs, so treat it as a possible aggravator. The earlier deliberate-pre-scale guess is SUPERSEDED - no code was found doing it and the stale-chip path explains the data without it; do not start from it. Repro plan in brief.md: check generationSettings.mediaItems in the new sidecar first, clean state vs after deleting a lineage entry.

NEGATIVE CONTROL - did NOT reproduce on a clean run, which kills the pre-scale theory outright. Fresh source t2i_038 (768x1344), factor 1.5, Use Grid on: the staged asset handed to the graph measured 768x1344 (its TRUE size, hash 9d52e898...) and the output was 1152x2016 - exactly 1.5x. So media staging does NOT resize; a normal run stages the source at native size. That leaves the stale-reference path as the only remaining explanation for the four bad runs, which all pointed at hash 1ed8902c... measuring 1152x2016. Bug is TRIGGER-DEPENDENT, not always-on: a clean session upscales correctly, so repro needs the trigger (entry deletion in the lineage, possibly with a concurrent browser generation). Diagnostic that worked: compare generationSettings.mediaItems in the sidecar against the selected item's own file, and measure the staged asset's PNG header - the size of the staged file is the tell.
